clue.text: Blubber about pound sterling being low

indicators.note: about says the word for blubber goes round the money abbreviation

parts.note: blubber is the fat of whales and seals
L is the old abbreviation for a pound in British money, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone weeps because the British currency has fallen in value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blubber' reads as the verb to cry, but it is the noun, whale fat. 'about' wraps it round L, the pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a note that is low in pitch, or spirits that are low, can be called flat.

clue.text: Asian destination not good for climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
not says the abbreviation for good is absent from the word

parts.note: a goal is the place you aim to reach

explanation.surface: A place in Asia turns out to be poor for mountaineering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not good' removes G from GOAL to leave OAL, and 'climbing' turns that upside down in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Lao are a people of South-East Asia, chiefly in Laos, so one of them is an Asian.

clue.text: Skin complaint developed by auntie, not for all to see

indicators.note: developed by says the relative's letters grow into a new arrangement
not says the film-certificate letter is taken away before the rearranging

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for all

explanation.surface: An aunt has come out with a rash that she keeps covered up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not for all to see' removes U (the British film rating for universal viewing) from AUNTIE, leaving ANTIE, which 'developed by' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical term: it is the name for ringworm, a fungal infection of the skin.

clue.text: Us magazine owner is late

definitions.meaning: whimsically, the proprietor of the American weekly called Time is the person standing at the back of it, supporting it
running after the hour that was planned

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom and pun: the phrase means running late, and read literally it places a proprietor at the back of an American news weekly.

clue.text: Empty boudoir on top of hotel disguised this?

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece on top is written first, above the other
an emptied word keeps only its first and last letters
something disguised has its appearance altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bare bedroom upstairs in a hotel was a cover for a house of ill repute.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer, with 'this' pointing at it; 'Empty', 'on top of' and 'disguised' also do the building, so every word works twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole-clue description: a house of prostitution might well hide behind a hotel front with a boudoir upstairs.

clue.text: Own, most recent software to settle an argument?

parts.note: to own something is to have it
the most recent one is the last one
Word is Microsoft's word-processing program

explanation.surface: Buying the newest program is proposed as the way to end a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Own' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to possess; 'software' is a brand name, Microsoft Word.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: whoever makes the final remark in a dispute closes it.

clue.text: Standard reply half ignored some French people

parts.note: a norm is a standard or usual level

indicators.note: half ignored means only the first half of the word for a reply is kept

parts.note: an answer is a reply

explanation.surface: A stock response is only partly heeded by a group of people from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half ignored' keeps ANS, the first half of ANSWER.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the people of Normandy are one group of the French.

clue.text: Excited mates left for a foursome?

indicators.note: excited letters are agitated and jump about into a new order

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Thrilled friends set off to make up a group of four.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excited' is the anagram signal and 'left' reads as departed but is the nautical side. A foursome is a golf match between two pairs, hence the question mark for an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: foursomes golf is played by two pairs, each pair a side working together.

clue.text: Pamper model coldly treated

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the two words' letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spoils a fashion model who has been given the cold shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges MODEL COLDLY; the surface makes it sound like unkind handling, the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both verbs mean to indulge or overprotect someone.

clue.text: Carried on at first in large island

parts.note: borne is the past participle of bear, meaning carried

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word just before it

explanation.surface: Someone kept going for a while on a big island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carried on' reads as one phrasal verb but splits: 'Carried' is BORNE and 'on at first' gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is the third-largest island in the world, in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Loose Arab veil can be changed

indicators.note: loose letters are not fixed in place, so they can be rearranged

explanation.surface: A loosely worn Arab face covering is one that may be swapped for another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' rearranges ARAB VEIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something described this way is liable to alter or be altered.

clue.text: Boater's almost drifting, eh?

indicators.note: almost means the word for drifting loses its last letter

parts.note: stray as an adjective means wandering or drifting, as a stray boat
eh? and what? are both ways of asking someone to repeat themselves

explanation.surface: Someone in a boat has nearly floated away, hasn't he?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boater' reads as a person in a boat but is the stiff summer hat. 'almost' trims STRAY to STRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a boater is a stiff flat-topped hat made of plaited straw.

clue.text: Put one in the picture about healing

indicators.note: Put ... in says the single letter is placed inside the rearranged words
about means the letters of the two words before it are moved around

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: Tell somebody the full facts about how recovery works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges THE PICTURE into THERPEUTIC, and 'Put one in' adds A inside it. 'Put in the picture' reads as the idiom for informing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as an adjective: a treatment with curative effect is described this way.

clue.text: Jenny taking state tests

indicators.note: taking means the animal's name takes the other word inside it

parts.note: a jenny is a female donkey, an ass
to state something is to say it

explanation.surface: A girl called Jenny sits official exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jenny' looks like a girl's name but is a female donkey, and 'state' is the verb, not a country; 'taking' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: as verb or noun, these are analyses of a metal or ore to determine its quality.

clue.text: New out, coloured nets to catch Scottish island fish

indicators.note: to catch says the outer letters trap the island's name between them

parts.note: red is one colour, so coloured can stand for it here

indicators.note: out says the abbreviation for new is removed from the phrase

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new, as in NT
Mull is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: Fresh dyed nets are put out to land fish off a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New out' reads as freshly launched, but it removes one letter from the two words that follow before 'to catch' makes them trap the Hebridean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: these are reddish sea fish prized as food.

clue.text: Port is behind a lot of cereal outside

indicators.note: outside says the shortened grain goes round the other word
a lot of means most of the grain's name, all but its last letter

parts.note: millet is a cereal grain
arse is British slang for the behind, the buttocks

explanation.surface: A harbour lies just beyond great fields of grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims MILLET to MILLE, which goes 'outside' ARSE, British slang for the backside. 'behind' looks like a preposition but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is France's great Mediterranean harbour city.

clue.text: Get a steer on county in brief

parts.note: a steer is a young castrated bull, an ox
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wants quick guidance about a county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get a steer' reads as getting guidance, but a steer is a bullock. The answer is the short form of Oxfordshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation: it is the shortened Latin name used for Oxfordshire, an English shire.

clue.text: Having taken bush's lead, former PM's in retreat

indicators.note: having taken away says the single letter is removed from the name

parts.note: Tony Blair was British Prime Minister from 1997 to 2007

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: After following the American president's direction, an ex-premier is backing down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having taken bush's lead' removes B from BLAIR, the British Prime Minister who followed President Bush into Iraq. 'retreat' is a noun, a hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a den or hideaway where one withdraws from the world.

clue.text: Because one enemy lawyer holds back appeal, it creates a stink

indicators.note: holds says the run of pieces takes the turned word inside it

parts.note: as can mean because
a is the indefinite article, meaning one
a foe is an enemy
DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

indicators.note: back means the word for appeal is written backwards

parts.note: it is an old term for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A hostile barrister delays an appeal, and that causes a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds back appeal' reads as delaying a court case, but 'back' is a reversal of the old slang for sex appeal and 'holds' places it inside the run of other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: it is a pungent, foul-smelling plant resin used as a spice in Indian cooking.

clue.text: Welcome support mostly relating to ancient Iranian language

parts.note: ave is the Latin greeting hail, a welcome

indicators.note: mostly means the word for support loses its last letter

parts.note: a stand is a support, as for a lamp or a music score

explanation.surface: Encouraging backing is given largely for work on an old Persian tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims STAND to STAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical adjective: it describes the old tongue of the Zoroastrian scriptures of Persia.

clue.text: Spoken about young woman in ring road

indicators.note: about says the word for spoken goes round the other word

parts.note: oral means spoken rather than written
bit is dated British slang for a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: People are talking about a girl seen on the bypass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoken' looks like a homophone signal, but it is a plain synonym; 'about' is the container signal, round dated British slang for a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: British usage: a motorway circling a city is called this, as London's M25 is.

clue.text: Harsh cut taken by police finally

indicators.note: taken by places the first piece beside the letter that follows

parts.note: to sever is to cut through

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: The police force has in the end accepted a brutal budget reduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harsh cut' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'Harsh' alone and 'cut' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both adjectives describe stern or punishing treatment.

clue.text: Bill, not at home ringing about low stool

parts.note: a tab is a bill run up at a bar

indicators.note: ringing means forming a ring round the other piece

parts.note: someone not at home is out
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Bill is away and phones to ask about a small seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' reads as telephoning but is the container signal, and 'about' is not an indicator here but a piece in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionary sense: it is a small drum-shaped seat without back or arms.

clue.text: French friend is after thickly skinned cucumber, acquired taste perhaps

indicators.note: is after says the French word follows the other letters
thickly skinned means a thick layer of letters is peeled from each side, leaving only the centre

parts.note: ami is the French word for friend

explanation.surface: A pal from France wants a tough-skinned cucumber, not something everyone likes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thickly skinned' is a novel signal: a thin skin would be one letter each side, a thick one takes three, leaving the centre pair; 'is after' sets the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is the savoury fifth basic flavour, alongside sweet, sour, salt and bitter.

clue.text: What could make you tilt toes if badly fitted?

definitions.text: What could make you tilt toes if badly fitted?

indicators.note: badly fitted says the letters of the two words are put together wrongly, in another order

explanation.surface: A high-heeled shoe of the wrong size forces the foot forward.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'badly fitted' rearranges TILT TOES, and the result is a shoe that does just that.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole-clue description: a spike-heeled shoe pitches the foot forward onto its front.

clue.text: The small church specified gets top-level cover

parts.note: with 'The' before it: the one specified is that one, a demonstrative pointing at a named thing
Ch is the short form of church

explanation.surface: A particular little chapel is given the best insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ... specified' together mean THAT, with the church's abbreviation tucked between them in the clue. 'top-level cover' is roofing, not insurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a roof of straw or reeds covers the highest part of a house.

clue.text: Not entirely appreciated us agency

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the word is used, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: Our bureau is only partly valued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' takes three consecutive letters from inside 'appreciated'. 'us' is really US, American.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is America's foreign intelligence service.

clue.text: Heard monitor not working for movie star

indicators.note: heard means the phrase is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a monitor is a screen, and one not working is idle

explanation.surface: A film actor is told the display has broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' makes SCREEN IDLE sound like the answer; only the second word changes spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a film actor adored by the public.

clue.text: Religious leader's obscure stuff, heads scratched

indicators.note: heads scratched means the first letter of each of the two words is struck out

parts.note: dim means obscure or hard to make out
to jam something in is to stuff it in

explanation.surface: A cleric's teaching is so hard to follow that people are left puzzled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads scratched' strikes D from DIM and J from JAM, leaving IM and AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: he is the man who leads prayers in a mosque.
